tg.metaDescription.en: Tune FancyUI's OKLCh design tokens live and copy the CSS into your app.

tg.intro.en: Tune FancyUI's design tokens and watch the components react in real time. When it looks right, copy the generated CSS into your app's stylesheet (e.g. src/app.css). Colors use the OKLCh color space; the rainbow palette uses HSL. For the full token reference, see <link>Theming</link>.

tg.beamDesc.context: Caption of a preview card whose animated border follows the two tuned colors. {primary} and {accent} are the translated labels of tg.primary and tg.accent. The arrow shows direction from the first colour to the second and is not mirrored in right-to-left text: in Arabic and Persian use the left-pointing arrow, or reword without one.

install.lead.en: Add FancyUI to a SvelteKit project in three steps: install the package, import the stylesheet, render a component.

install.prerequisites.body.en: FancyUI targets current toolchains. Check these three before installing.

install.prerequisites.card1.desc.en: Components are written with runes, so Svelte 5 is required. Svelte 4 projects will not compile them.

install.prerequisites.card2.desc.en: Styling relies on Tailwind v4 utilities and CSS custom properties.

install.prerequisites.card3.desc.en: Required by the current build tooling FancyUI is tested against.

install.steps.body.en: Pick your package manager, wire up the stylesheet, then render your first component.

install.step1.desc.en: One package for every component. Switch tabs to copy the command for your package manager.

install.step2.desc.en: Add the FancyUI stylesheet right after your Tailwind import.

install.step2.caption.en: In your global stylesheet, usually src/app.css.

install.step3.desc.en: Import from the package root and drop it into your markup.

install.tailwind.body.en: FancyUI is built on Tailwind CSS v4, which is configured in CSS instead of a JavaScript config file. If Tailwind already works in your project, there is nothing else to configure.

install.tailwind.order.en: Import order matters: Tailwind first, FancyUI second. Place the FancyUI import before your own @custom-variant dark, otherwise FancyUI's replaces yours.

install.tailwind.note.en: The entry provides default colour tokens (background, primary, border and the rest) and a dark variant. Your own :root and .dark blocks override them: redefine the CSS variables and your values win.

install.usage.body.en: Every component is a named export of the package root, so there are no per-component import paths to remember.

install.usage.note.en: Each component's page lists its props, live examples and accessibility notes.

install.typescript.body.en: Prop types are exported next to each component, so you can type wrappers and shared presets.

install.typescript.note.en: Types ship inside the package. There is no separate types package to install.

install.peerDeps.body.en: FancyUI expects these to already exist in your project:

install.peerDeps.bundled.en: A few components need extra runtime libraries. These ship with the package, so there is nothing more to install:

install.peerDeps.bundledNote.en: They are only pulled in by the components that use them.

install.nextSteps.components.desc.en: {count} components with live previews, props and copy-paste examples.

install.nextSteps.theming.desc.en: Override the design tokens so every component matches your brand in light and dark mode.

theming.lead.en: Every FancyUI component reads its colors, radii and timings from CSS custom properties in the OKLCh color space — override a token and the whole library follows.

theming.generator.body.en: Prefer to tune it visually? The Theme Generator adjusts these tokens with live sliders and hands you the CSS.

theming.cssSetup.body.en: Import the FancyUI stylesheet in your app's global CSS, usually src/app.css:

theming.colors.body.en: All colors use the OKLCh color space for perceptually uniform gradients:

theming.colors.note.en: Token names follow the widely used semantic convention (background, foreground, primary, …), so an existing theme with the same variable names drops in unchanged.

theming.dark.body.en: Dark mode follows the operating-system preference by default. Put the .dark class on <html> or any ancestor to force dark, or .light to force light; the dark: utilities and every token follow. To customise the dark values, override them under .dark:

theming.easing.body.en: Easing curves are tokens too, shared by every component transition:

theming.rainbow.body.en: Used by RainbowButton, GradientButton and other gradient effects:

theming.customizing.body.en: Override any token in your own CSS to change the look:

theming.customizing.note.en: Tokens cascade: override them globally in :root, or scope them to a wrapper element to theme a single section.

theming.nextSteps.generator.desc.en: Tune every token with live sliders and copy the finished CSS.

theming.nextSteps.components.desc.en: See the tokens at work across the full component gallery.

retro.tagline.en: Animated components for Svelte 5 — copy-paste friendly.

comp.snippetSvelteOnly.en: A full example for this framework is not written yet; only the Svelte version has one for now.

comp.markdownSvelteOnly.en: The Markdown export describes the Svelte version only.

comp.apiNoticeReact.en: This API reference uses the Svelte names. In React, class becomes className, on* handlers are camelCase (onclick becomes onClick) and snippets become ReactNode props or render functions.

comp.apiNoticeVue.en: This API reference uses the Svelte names. In Vue, snippets become slots and bindable props become v-model:name.

install.prerequisites.card1.desc.react.en: Supports React 18 and 19. Components ship as client modules, so Server Components can import them directly.

install.prerequisites.card1.desc.vue.en: Components are Vue 3.5 single-file components, so Vue 3.5.2 or later is required.

install.astro.heading.context: Installation page, heading of the Astro section (shown with the Svelte framework only). Product name.

install.astro.body.en: FancyUI runs in Astro through the official Svelte integration, with no extra package. Add the integration and Tailwind, install the package, then import the stylesheet from step 2 in your layout.
install.astro.body.context: Astro section intro, above the install commands. 'step 2' is the numbered stylesheet step earlier on the page.

install.astro.static.en: A component used without a {directive} directive renders to HTML and CSS and ships no JavaScript. BorderBeam, Marquee, Meteors, and buttons without a handler work this way.
install.astro.static.context: Astro section, above a static example. {directive} is the code token client:* (an Astro attribute).

install.astro.island.en: To hydrate a component, import it in a local {svelte} file and put the directive on that file. Handlers, state and snippets go in that file too: from {astro}, only the default slot reaches an island.
install.astro.island.context: Astro section, above the island example. {svelte} is '.svelte' and {astro} is '.astro' (file extensions). An island is Astro's hydrated component.

install.astro.why.en: Do not put the directive on a component imported from the package root in an {astro} file: the island would load the whole library. For one RainbowButton island, the local file ships {wrapped} of JavaScript and the package root {barrel}, with three.js and GSAP, a chunk then shared by every island page of the site.
install.astro.why.context: Astro section warning. {astro} is '.astro'; {wrapped} and {barrel} are measured sizes such as '88 KB (32 KB gzip)'.

install.astro.router.en: {router} is supported: islands are destroyed on each navigation, and {persist} keeps one alive across pages.
install.astro.router.context: Astro section. {router} is 'ClientRouter' and {persist} is 'transition:persist' (Astro code tokens).

install.astro.versions.en: Tested with astro {astroVersion} and @astrojs/svelte {integrationVersion}, which need Node {node} or later.
install.astro.versions.context: Astro section caption. {astroVersion}, {integrationVersion} and {node} are version numbers.
